quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes exhaust fumes from your vehicle. A leak allows dangerous carbon monoxide gas to enter the passenger area. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter the intersection until you can drive completely across it.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter the intersection until you can drive completely across it.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: On a highway, a single broken white line means:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to yield the right-of-way. Slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you. Stop if needed before proceeding.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly frustrates other drivers and can cause them to make dangerous passing moves. The safest approach is to drive with traffic flow, within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon. Move to the left lane.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign with black markings tells you that a lane is ending ahead. Traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are present.
Always stop before entering the sidewalk or street.
Expect pedestrians to yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always stop before entering the sidewalk or street.
questions.explanation: Always stop before driving onto a sidewalk or street from an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic on the street have the right-of-way.

questions.question: A yellow left turn arrow means:

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
Your protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic before making your left turn.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points, but first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones along roads. These signs are usually diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols and warn that workers are present on or near the highway.

questions.question: What must you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Stop completely. Check for people and cars crossing.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Check for people and cars crossing.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely. Look for people walking and cars crossing the intersection. Wait until it is clear before you go.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against your seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting other cars.

questions.question: What is true about crosswalks?

options.text: They always have painted lines on the road.
They always have vertical painted lines on the road.
They are never marked.
They may have painted lines or no lines at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may have painted lines or no lines at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist with or without painted lines. You must stop behind the crosswalk to let people cross.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes it easier to see crossing traffic.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As you go faster, you see less around you. You must pay extra attention to dangers.

questions.question: How fast should you always travel?

options.text: At the same speed as the cars around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match the road conditions, weather, and speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the middle of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic goes in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic goes in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic goes in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic goes in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic goes in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted across traffic lanes?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted at intersections and crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: What do drivers need for interstate driving?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at high speeds.
Constant alertness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert at all times and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and against the law to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no one can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What can you do at a roadway with a single broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross the centerline to change lanes.
You can only change lanes from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean traffic moves in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal works the same as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic pass first.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on your right has the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: A transit bus is signaling to get back on the road after stopping. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a transit bus that is signaling to return to the road. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus back into traffic safely.
